topic: Quadratic coefficients from x-intercepts with an integer leading coefficient
problem: A quadratic function f is defined by f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, where a is an integer greater than 1. The graph of y = f(x) in the xy-plane has x-intercepts at (-2, 0) and (8, 0). Which of the following could be the value of a + b?

bad.why: Only two points are given for three unknowns; the fit is underdetermined and lands on an arbitrary, usually non-integer a.
Restricting a>1 inside a regression is not a constraint; it still returns a non-integer a instead of testing whole numbers.
Testing the choices needs the hand-derived relation a+b=-5a first; the choices cannot be plugged in directly.

algebraFirst.description: Writes f(x)=a(x+2)(x-8), expands to ax^2-6ax-16a so a+b=-5a, then checks which choice is -5 times an integer greater than 1.

explanationNotes: Explain that x-intercepts at -2 and 8 mean f(x)=a(x+2)(x-8), and that f(1)-f(0) equals a+b because f(1)=a+b+c while f(0)=c. Because a must be a whole number bigger than 1, a list of a values shows every possible a+b (-10, -15, -20, ...), and -15 is the only one among the choices.
notes: f(x)=a(x+2)(x-8), so a+b=-5a. With a an integer >= 2 (an integer list a=[2...10]), only -15 (a=3) is achievable among the choices. This is the exact reported variance bug: a run that used an inequality-restricted underdetermined regression here would land on a wrong, non-integer a.
